- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) in recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast to reflect bearish pressure.  
- Model often underestimates sharp upward moves (spikes) — especially after sentiment turns positive — and fails to capture early momentum.  
- Model shows persistent downward bias in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — adjust upward if sentiment shifts to positive mid-horizon.  
- Overshoots after strong upward spikes (e.g., 70→80) — cap forecast at 10–15% below peak if sentiment remains neutral or cooling.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is trending sharply upward, reduce slope slightly if sentiment turns neutral or negative.  
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often lag by 1–2 price points in bullish regimes — add 1–2% buffer if sentiment is rising.  
- If sentiment is flat or mixed, model tends to overfit recent noise — smooth forecast curve and avoid sharp turns.
